title: Pod eviction surge after VPC EIP reconciliation — incident notes
body:
Summary:
A cluster-wide spike of Pod evictions and transient DNS failures occurred for ~18 minutes on 2024-11-07 09:12–09:30 UTC. Root cause appears to be an automated VPC Elastic IP (EIP) reconciliation job that re-bound public IPs to different ENIs across multiple worker subnets, triggering a burst of CNI reattach/iptables churn and host-level NAT table exhaustion on affected nodes. The result: rapid liveness probe failures, kubelet-initiated eviction waves, and application disruptions for a subset of latency-sensitive services (ingress proxies and batch workers).

Impact:
- Time window: 09:12–09:30 UTC
- Affected clusters: us-west-2-prod-primary (mixed instance types, GPU and CPU pools)
- Scope: ~120 nodes (out of 2,400) showed high eviction counts (p95 evictions/node increased from 0 to 37 in the window).
- Customer-facing impact: transient request errors (~5–10% error amplification on 3 services behind ingress) and increased tail latency for embedding inference paths for ~12 minutes.

High-level timeline (collected from alerts, cloud events, and node logs):
- 09:11:48 UTC — scheduled orchestration job 'vpc-eip-reconcile' starts (internal infra service).
- 09:12:06 UTC — multiple EIP reassignments occur within the same AZ over ~40s window. Cloud event stream shows ~280 EIP-change events across the AZs in that minute.
- 09:12:15 UTC — nodes in subnets with high EIP churn start logging cni-plugin errors: "failed to apply iptables rules: resource temporarily unavailable" and "netlink: message dropped".
- 09:12:40 UTC — kube-proxy and kubelet logs show high iptables/conntrack churn and RETRY loops during pod networking updates.
- 09:13:10 UTC — liveness probes begin failing for pods with UDP-heavy/DNS calls; kubelet starts evicting pods as node-level pressure metrics cross eviction thresholds (ephemeral-storage and network-related backpressure flags).
- 09:18:00 UTC — infra team pauses the reconcile job; number of new EIP changes drops.
- 09:22:00 UTC — conntrack table usage begins to decline on affected nodes; iptables update latency returns to normal.
- 09:30:00 UTC — eviction rate returns to baseline; incident resolved for most services.

Root cause analysis (hypothesis + evidence):
1) Trigger: a late-night maintenance trigger allowed an EIP reconciliation job to run during a production traffic spike window. The job, when executing many reassignments in quick succession within a single AZ, caused large bursts of ENI detach/attach and public IP translation state changes. Evidence: cloud event logs show ~280 EIP reassign events within a ~60s window correlated with our scheduled job ID.

2) Node-level effect: rapid sequence of ENI state changes caused the CNI (our vendor plugin) to reprogram interfaces and iptables rules repeatedly. Each interface reprogram step enqueues iptables modifications and conntrack flushes; under burst it hit the node kernel limits (conntrack and netlink queues) and triggered resource contention. Evidence: node syslogs and dmesg show netlink queue drops and conntrack NOTIFY flood warnings; kernel messages include 'nf_conntrack: table full' on several hosts.

3) Kubelet/Kube-proxy fallout: iptables reflows increased pod networking latency (DNS retries, TCP connect stalls). Health checks timed out and pods were evicted when resource pressure thresholds were exceeded. Kubelet eviction metrics and kube-apiserver event stream show eviction reasons including "NodeHasNoDiskPressure" misreported alongside network-related probe failures (a combination of ephemeral disk backpressure and probe timeout misclassification under high CNI CPU usage).

4) Contributing factor: reconciliation job had no rate-limiting per-AZ and assumed infra-level NAT and conntrack capacity was elastic. We lacked a guardrail to detect when netlink or conntrack saturation reaches unsafe levels. Also, runbooks did not specify pausing at first signs of kernel NAT saturation.

Immediate mitigation taken during incident:
- Infra runbook executed: paused vpc-eip-reconcile job at 09:18 by cancelling orchestration task.
- SRE team manually cordoned the most-impacted node groups to stop scheduling new pods while allowing draining of in-flight work.
- Ran 'echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_acct' and increased conntrack hashsize on a handful of worst-affected nodes as a tactical measure (note: requires reboot for persistent change — used only as short-term relief).
- Temporarily increased kubelet probe timeouts for the ingress proxy Deployment via emergency patch to reduce evictions while conntrack backlog drained.

Observations from metrics/logs for debugging:
- conntrack_table_size (node exporter): spiked to 98–100% on impacted nodes; normal baseline 12–18%.
- netlink_rx_drops: measurable increase coincident with EIP events.
- iptables-apply-latency (custom metric): median jumped from ~8ms to ~650ms during the EIP burst window.
- kube-proxy restart events: none, but high CPU in the CNI plugin observed.

What went wrong in runbook/process:
- SRE playbook lacked an automated detector for conntrack saturation or rapid netlink error rates. We relied on pod-level health alerts which are downstream symptoms.
- Rate-limits and safety checks in the EIP reconciliation service are conservative for steady-state but do not currently enforce a per-AZ or per-subnet smoothing window when reassignments are scheduled en masse.
- No cross-team paging rule existed between infra job owners and on-call SREs for bulk infra changes that affect ENI/network state.

Action items (short/medium/long term):
- Short (hotfixes, due 2024-11-12):
  - Add a simple guard in vpc-eip-reconcile to limit EIPs re-bound to max 8 per 5m per-AZ and implement exponential backoff on failure. (Owner: infra-svc-team)
  - Add an automated alert: node_conntrack_utilization > 80% for more than 60s -> page oncall-sre and infra-owner. (Owner: eng-sre)
  - Update SRE emergency runbook with explicit steps for conntrack troubleshooting and tactical knob list (probe timeout tweak, cordon/uncordon, conntrack hashsize bump procedure). (Owner: Aisha Khan)

- Medium (Q1 2025 work):
  - Implement a non-disruptive reconciliation mode which gates changes if any node in a target AZ reports conntrack/util or netlink drop signals. (Owner: infra-engineering)
  - Evaluate CNI plugin settings and kernel-side tunables to increase graceful handling of ENI rapid attach/detach sequences. (Owner: platform-networking)
  - Add a canary policy for infra jobs: run first 1–2 EIP reassigns in a canary subnet and only continue if node-level metrics remain within thresholds. (Owner: infra-svc-team)

- Long (Architecture, FY25):
  - Design a per-AZ quota and smoothing service for infra-level public-IP changes to avoid concentrated bursts.
  - Explore offloading NAT state to managed NAT gateways where possible to decouple node conntrack dependency for public translation.

Runbook additions/changes (draft wording to insert):
- Detecting a conntrack saturation event:
  - Metric to watch: node_exporter.conntrack_count / node_exporter.conntrack_max (alert > 0.8 for > 60s)
  - Secondary signals: netlink_rx_drops > 5/s, iptables_apply_latency_p95 > 200ms, CNI CPU > 75% for 1m.
  - If detected: pause any ongoing infra reconciliation jobs targeting this AZ, cordon the most-impacted node pool, and increase probe timeouts for stateful services if safe to do so.

- Emergency commands (tactical, non-persistent):
  - Check conntrack: sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count and /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
  - Drain backlog: sudo conntrack -L | head -n 50 (inspect), sudo conntrack -F (use with extreme caution, will drop existing connections)
  - Increase hashsize (requires caution): echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max (not persisted across reboot)

Post-incident notes and unresolved questions:
- Why did kubelet report diskPressure-related eviction signals alongside the network-induced probe failures? Hypothesis: kernel CPU/interrupt saturation made kubelet's housekeeping appear delayed and false-positive for disk pressure. Need to add instrumentation to distinguish disk IO queues vs. kubelet internal backlog. (Action: SRE instrumentation spike story)
- Does our current CNI vendor have recommended knobs for high ENI churn? Contact vendor support and test recommended settings in a staging cluster. (Owner: platform-networking)

Appendix — useful commands/log snippets:
- Cloud event query (example): aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=ec2.amazonaws.com --start-time 2024-11-07T09:10:00Z --end-time 2024-11-07T09:20:00Z | grep AllocateAddress
- Node diagnostics:
  - sudo journalctl -u kubelet -o short-iso --since "2024-11-07 09:00:00" | egrep "conntrack|iptables|CNI|netlink"
  - sudo dmesg | egrep "nf_conntrack|netlink|iptables"
- Metric slices to review (Grafana): node/conntrack-utilization (by node), cni/iptables-apply-latency, infra/vpc-eip-change-rate (custom infra metric by AZ)

Worklog and owners (who did what during incident):
- 09:16–09:20 — Marco Liang triaged node logs and noticed nf_conntrack table full messages; escalated to infra-svc-team.
- 09:18 — Infra-svc-team paused reconcile job (Mitigation).
- 09:19–09:25 — Sophia Martinez applied emergency probe-timeout patch to ingress proxies.
- 09:25–09:30 — Ethan Park cordoned affected node pools and validated steady-state metrics.

Next steps before finalizing postmortem:
- Reproduce a scaled-down EIP-burst in staging to validate our conntrack alerts and guardrails. (Owner: infra-svc-team)
- Schedule vendor support call with CNI provider and share logs. (Owner: platform-networking)
- Add the short-term runbook edits and communicate to oncall rotation. (Owner: Aisha Khan)

Status: draft — this doc will be turned into a formal postmortem after the confirmatory staging tests and vendor feedback are complete.
